_phase_tag: PRESS STATION — bearing cup orientation (TIMKEN side)
_step_title: Steps 1–2 — big & small bearing cup orientation on the cover
_recorded_by: Comer line mechanical engineer (errors_pinion_guide_for_KB.txt), relayed by Omnia 2026-07-14
_verified_by: line mechanical engineer 2026-07-14: orientation of both cups confirmed on the line; reference photos re-shot to match. Curated source docs/source-material/errors_pinion_guide_for_KB.txt.

facts.fact: The BIG bearing cup cod.248114A1 (Step 1, pressed onto the cover) is assembled with the TIMKEN stamped side facing UP — the engraved TIMKEN maker text must be visible on the up-face when the cup sits on the punch fixture. If the bare bright tapered raceway (no lettering) is facing up, the cup is INVERTED: stop and flip it before pressing. The press flags an inverted cup out-of-range, but once pressed wrong it is incredibly difficult to remove and usually damages the part.
facts.applies_when: step 1 — big bearing cup on cover

citation.transcript_quote: The Bearing cup cod. 248114A1 assembled TIMKEN side facing UP

facts.fact: The SMALL bearing cup cod.191440A1 (Step 2, fixed on the cover) is assembled with the TIMKEN stamped side facing DOWN — the bright smooth tapered raceway faces up and NO lettering is visible on the up-face. If the stamped TIMKEN text is visible facing up, the cup is INVERTED: stop and flip it before pressing.
facts.applies_when: step 2 — small bearing cup on cover

citation.transcript_quote: the small bearing cup cod. 191440A1 assembled TIMKEN facing down

facts.fact: The two bearing cups use OPPOSITE orientation conventions and this is the trap: big cup 248114A1 goes TIMKEN side UP, small cup 191440A1 goes TIMKEN side DOWN. Never carry one cup's rule onto the other — check which cup is in hand (outer diameter / bin label / current step) before judging its orientation. A fast visual tell photographed side-by-side: the big cup's stamped TIMKEN rim is a visibly THICKER/WIDER flat annulus than the small cup's narrow stamped band. The big cup's correct pose (TIMKEN face up on the fixture) is also what the Phase-1 'INSERT BEARING CUP' work-instruction photo (Phase1.pdf) shows. Inverted cup/cone assembly is one of the two most error-prone tasks on this station.

citation.transcript_quote: The Bearing cup cod. 248114A1 assembled TIMKEN side facing UP and the small bearing cup cod. 191440A1 assembled TIMKEN facing down.
